findings.title: `shell=True` enables shell injection
findings.justification: With shell=True the command string is interpreted by the shell, so any interpolated value can inject further commands.
findings.suggestion: Pass a list of arguments and leave shell=False.

findings.title: Mutable default argument is shared across calls
findings.justification: Default arguments are evaluated once at function definition, so the same list/dict is reused by every call and accumulates state.
findings.suggestion: Default to `None` and build the container inside the function.

findings.title: Synchronous HTTP call inside a coroutine blocks the event loop
findings.justification: `requests` is blocking; called from a coroutine it serialises all concurrent tasks on the same loop.
findings.suggestion: Use an async client, or wrap the call in `asyncio.to_thread`.

findings.title: Blocking `time.sleep` inside a coroutine stalls the event loop
findings.justification: time.sleep blocks the thread running the loop, so every other task on that loop is frozen for the duration: the concurrency is fake.
findings.suggestion: Use `await asyncio.sleep(...)`.

findings.title: `eval`/`exec` on runtime data is a code-execution risk
findings.justification: If any part of the argument comes from user input, request data or a file, this executes arbitrary code in the process.
findings.suggestion: Use `ast.literal_eval`, `json.loads`, or an explicit dispatch dict.

findings.title: Lock acquired without a guaranteed release
findings.justification: If the guarded block raises, `.release()` is never reached and every other thread blocks on that lock forever: a deadlock.
findings.suggestion: Use the lock as a context manager (`with lock:`) or try/finally.

findings.title: Bare `except:` swallows every exception
findings.justification: A bare except also catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, so the process stops being interruptible and real errors are hidden.
findings.suggestion: Catch the specific exception, or `except Exception:` at minimum.
